chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Sayaba ibn Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abdul Raheem al-Qasir, who said:

The governor sent for a man from the progeny of Abu Talib regarding a felony. He passed by Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Follow him with a carnelian ring.' So a carnelian ring was brought to him, and he did not see any abhorrence in it.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the carnelian ring in the context of the Ahl al-Bayt and judicial proceedings?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the practical efficacy of wearing a carnelian ring (*khatam 'aqiq*) as a symbol of status and divine favor, ensuring the Ahl al-Bayt member was treated with due respect by the governor. The Imam’s silent approval (*la yara makruhan*) highlights the Shia scholarly view that such adornments are not merely decorative but carry spiritual and social weight, serving as a means of *shifa* or *barakah* in worldly affairs. This incident underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition (*sunnah*) within the Imams' lives, linking material objects to spiritual authority.
